claim: Prp43 is a DEAH-box helicase that is a key player in pre-mRNA splicing and the maturation of rRNAs.
source: The DEAH-box helicase Prp43 is a key player in pre-mRNA splicing as well as the maturation of rRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characterization of Prp43's biological roles, drawing on established scientific knowledge about this helicase.

claim: The exact modus operandi of Prp43 and all other spliceosomal DEAH-box RNA helicases is still elusive.
source: The exact modus operandi of Prp43 and of all other spliceosomal DEAH-box RNA helicases is still elusive.
evidence: This statement acknowledges a gap in current scientific understanding, representing the state of knowledge at the time of writing.

claim: Crystal structures of Prp43 complexes in different functional states were determined.
source: Here, we report crystal structures of Prp43 complexes in different functional states
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental crystallographic data for multiple Prp43 structures, as detailed in the Results section and supported by figures.

claim: The Prp43•ATP-analog•RNA complex shows the localization of the RNA inside a tunnel formed by the two RecA-like and C-terminal domains.
source: The Prp43•ATP-analog•RNA complex shows the localization of the RNA inside a tunnel formed by the two RecA-like and C-terminal domains.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- and shown in Figure 1d which displays the RNA-binding tunnel.

claim: In the ATP-bound state, the RNA-binding tunnel can be transformed into a groove prone for RNA binding by large rearrangements of the C-terminal domains.
source: In the ATP-bound state this tunnel can be transformed into a groove prone for RNA binding by large rearrangements of the C-terminal domains.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3- structures with the RNA-bound structure, as shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Conformational changes between the ATP- and ADP-bound states explain the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to RNA translocation, mainly mediated by a β-turn of the RecA1 domain containing the newly identified RF motif.
source: Several conformational changes between the ATP- and ADP-bound states explain the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to RNA translocation, mainly mediated by a β-turn of the RecA1 domain containing the newly identified RF motif.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparisons shown in Figures 6 and 7, and functional data from mutant analyses in Figure 4.

claim: The mechanism of Prp43 is clearly different from those of other RNA helicases.
source: This mechanism is clearly different to those of other RNA helicases.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparing Prp43 structures and functional data with MLE and other helicases, particularly regarding the Hook-Turn vs Hook-Loop mechanisms.

claim: SF1 and SF2 helicase superfamilies are monomeric, in contrast to SF3-SF6 members which assemble as hexamers.
source: Most members of the SF1 or SF2 are monomeric, in contrast to the members of SF3 to SF6 which assemble as hexamers
evidence: This is cited from Singleton et al., 2007, representing established knowledge in the helicase field.

claim: SF2 is the largest superfamily of helicases, comprising numerous RNA helicases with implications in various RNP metabolism pathways.
source: The SF2 is by far the largest superfamily, comprising a vast number of RNA helicases with implications in numerous RNP metabolism pathways, such as translation initiation and termination, pre-mRNA editing and splicing, mRNA export as well as ribosome biogenesis
evidence: This is cited from Ozgur et al., 2015, representing established knowledge about SF2 helicases.

claim: The C-terminal extension of DEAH-box helicases is highly conserved and composed of three domains: a winged helix (WH), a ratchet, and an oligosaccharide binding (OB) fold.
source: The C-terminal extension is highly conserved in DEAH-box helicases and is composed of three domains: a winged helix (WH), a ratchet and an oligosaccharide binding (OB) fold
evidence: This is cited from Walbott et al., 2010 and He et al., 2010, representing established structural knowledge.

claim: Prp43 acts at the latest stage of the splicing cycle and is required to dismantle the intron-lariat spliceosome into the excised lariat and the U2•U5•U6 snRNPs.
source: In the course of this process, Prp43 acts at the latest stage of the splicing cycle and it is required to dismantle the intron-lariat spliceosome into the excised lariat and the U2•U5•U6 snRNPs
evidence: This is cited from Arenas and Abelson, 1997 and Fourmann et al., 2013, 2016a, representing established knowledge about Prp43 function.

claim: The target substrate of Prp43 during splicing is the RNA network between the U2 snRNP and the branch site of the intron.
source: Recently, the target substrate of Prp43 during this process was revealed which is the RNA network between the U2 snRNP and the branch site of the intron
evidence: This is cited from Fourmann et al., 2016b, representing recent experimental findings.

claim: In the spliceosome, Prp43 was crosslinked exclusively to the pre-mRNA and not to any snRNAs.
source: Indeed, in the spliceosome, Prp43 was crosslinked exclusively to the pre-mRNA and not to any snRNAs.
evidence: This is cited from Fourmann et al., 2016b, representing experimental crosslinking data.

claim: Prp43 is involved in the maturation of 18S and 25S rRNAs with several reported binding sites on intermediates which vary in sequence.
source: Here, it is involved in the maturation of 18S and 25S rRNAs with several reported binding sites on intermediates which vary in sequence
evidence: This is cited from Lebaron et al., 2005 and Bohnsack et al., 2009, representing established knowledge about Prp43 in ribosome biogenesis.

claim: Prp43 is involved in the promotion of apoptosis.
source: Lately, the involvement of Prp43 in a third distinct cellular function was illuminated and it was unraveled that Prp43 is also involved in the promotion of apoptosis
evidence: This is cited from Heininger et al., 2016, representing recent findings about Prp43 function.

claim: G-patch proteins increase the NTPase and stimulate the helicase activity of Prp43.
source: Apart from being involved in recruitment, these G-patch proteins also increase the NTPase and stimulate the helicase activity of Prp43.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about G-patch protein function, cited from multiple sources in the manuscript.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, four out of five identified G-patch proteins interact with Prp43.
source: To date, in S. cerevisiae five G-patch proteins were identified out of which four interact with Prp43.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about yeast G-patch proteins, cited from multiple sources.

claim: In the context of splicing, Prp43 function is modulated by Ntr1.
source: In the context of splicing, Prp43 function is modulated by Ntr1 (Nineteen complex-related proteins 1)
evidence: This is cited from multiple sources (Tanaka et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2005, 2007; Boon et al., 2006).

claim: During rRNA maturation, Prp43 is associated with Pfa1 or Gno1.
source: During rRNA maturation, Prp43 is associated with Pfa1 (Prp forty-three associated 1) or Gno1 (G-patch nucleolar protein 1)
evidence: This is cited from Lebaron et al., 2005, 2009 and Bohnsack et al., 2009.

claim: The apoptotic function of Prp43 is implemented by the interaction with Cmg1.
source: Moreover, its apoptotic function is implemented by the interaction with Cmg1 (Cytoplasmic and mitochondrial G-patch protein 1)
evidence: This is cited from Heininger et al., 2016.

claim: The crystal structure of MLE with U10-RNA and ADP•AlF4- led to a proposed mechanism of how RNA is translocated through its interior tunnel driven by conformational changes of a Hook-Loop in the RecA2 domain.
source: The complex of MLE with a U10-RNA and ADP•AlF4- led to a proposed mechanism of how RNA is translocated through its interior tunnel driven by conformational changes of a Hook-Loop in the RecA2 domain
evidence: This is cited from Prabu et al., 2015, representing the proposed mechanism for MLE.

claim: Three crystal structures of Prp43 in the post-catalytic ADP-bound state have been available from S. cerevisiae or C. thermophilum prior to this study.
source: So far, three crystal structures of Prp43 in the post-catalytic ADP-bound state have been available from S. cerevisiae or C. thermophilum
evidence: This is cited from Walbott et al., 2010; He et al., 2010; Tauchert et al., 2016, representing prior structural work.

claim: The ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- complex structure was determined at 2.6 Å resolution.
source: Table 1 shows the resolution for ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- as 2.6 Å
evidence: This is experimental crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: ctPrp43 consists of six different domains: an N-terminal extension (residues 1–96), the RecA1 (97–273) and RecA2 (274–458) domains, and the C-terminal domains which were assigned as degenerate winged helix domain (459–526), ratchet-like domain (527–640) and oligosaccharide binding-fold domain (641–764).
source: ctPrp43 consists of six different domains: an N-terminal extension (residues 1–96), the RecA1 (97–273) and RecA2 (274–458) domains, and the C-terminal domains which were assigned as degenerate winged helix domain (459–526), ratchet-like domain (527–640) and oligosaccharide binding-fold domain (641–764)
evidence: This domain assignment is cited from Walbott et al., 2010 and He et al., 2010, and confirmed by the current structures.

claim: The 5' end of the RNA is located at the RecA2 domain and the 3' RNA end is situated at the RecA1 domain in the Prp43•RNA complex.
source: The 5' end of the RNA is located at the RecA2 domain and the 3' RNA end is situated at the RecA1 domain.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1c and 1e.

claim: For the first three nucleotides at the 5' end (U1–U3) of the bound RNA, two alternative conformations are observed.
source: For the first three nucleotides at the 5' end (U1–U3) two alternative conformations are observed
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The structure reveals the basis for the sequence-independent RNA binding of Prp43.
source: The structure reveals the basis for the sequence-independent RNA binding of Prp43 which is in line with previous biochemical data
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing lack of base-specific interactions, and is consistent with cited biochemical data from Fourmann et al., 2016b; Bohnsack et al., 2009; Tanaka and Schwer, 2006.

claim: Only 11 or 13 hydrogen bonds and ionic interactions between the RNA and Prp43 can be detected, depending on which of the two alternative RNA conformations is analyzed.
source: Depending on which of the two alternative RNA conformations is analyzed, only 11 or 13 hydrogen bonds and ionic interactions between the RNA and Prp43 can be detected
evidence: This is determined from the crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 1c and 1e.

claim: Most interactions between Prp43 and RNA are formed between the sugar-phosphate backbone of the RNA and the RecA1, RecA2 or the ratchet-like domain.
source: Most of these interactions are formed between the sugar-phosphate backbone of the RNA and the RecA1, RecA2 or the ratchet-like domain.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1c and 1e.

claim: The uracil moieties do not interact with the helicase with the exception of a hydrogen bond of U3 with the Ser 555 main-chain carboxyl group from the ratchet-like domain and a base stack between the U1 and Arg 562.
source: On the contrary, the uracil moieties do not interact with the helicase with the exception of a hydrogen bond of U3 with the Ser 555 main-chain carboxyl group from the ratchet-like domain and a base stack between the U1 and Arg 562 which only occurs in one of the two alternative conformations.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1c and 1e.

claim: Only four nucleotides (U4 to U7) are more tightly associated with Prp43.
source: In addition to the unspecific RNA-binding mode of Prp43, RNA binding appears to be transient, as only four nucleotides are more tightly associated with Prp43. In the crystal structure presented, this corresponds to the nucleotides U4 to U7.
evidence: This is inferred from the number of interactions and B-factors shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The first three nucleotides at the 5' end are weakly bound by Prp43 since only 2 (conf. B) and 3 (conf. A) interactions are detectable.
source: At the 5' end, the first three nucleotides are weakly bound by Prp43 since only 2 (conf. B) and 3 (conf. A) interactions are detectable, respectively.
evidence: This is determined from the crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 1e.

claim: The weak interaction of U1-U3 with Prp43 is additionally highlighted by elevated B-factors for this RNA region compared to the four other nucleotides.
source: The weak interaction is additionally highlighted by elevated B-factors for this RNA region compared to the four other nucleotides (see Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 displaying B-factor analysis.

claim: ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3- crystallized in two different crystal forms: orthorhombic space group P212121 (high resolution) and hexagonal space group P65 (low resolution).
source: ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) crystalized in the orthorhombic space group P212121 and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(LR) in the hexagonal space group P65.
evidence: This is experimental crystallographic data presented in Table 1 and Figure 2.

claim: The center of mass of the ratchet-like domain is shifted by 16.2 Å between ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) after alignment of the RecA-like domains.
source: Comparison between the ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- and the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structures after alignment of the RecA-like domains revealed that the center of mass of the ratchet-like domain is shifted by 16.2 Å
evidence: This is calculated from structural superposition of the crystal structures.

claim: The center of mass of the OB-fold domain is shifted by 14.1 Å between ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) after alignment of the RecA-like domains.
source: Comparison between the ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- and the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structures after alignment of the RecA-like domains revealed that... by 14.1 Å for the OB-fold domain.
evidence: This is calculated from structural superposition of the crystal structures.

claim: In the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(LR) complex structure, the center of mass shifts are 17.0 Å (ratchet-like) and 11.7 Å (OB-fold).
source: In the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(LR) complex structure, these values are equal to 17.0 Å (ratchet-like) and 11.7 Å (OB-fold), respectively.
evidence: This is calculated from structural superposition of the crystal structures.

claim: In the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structure, one inter-domain contact is present between the RecA2 (Asp 486) and the ratchet-like domain (Lys 605).
source: These two states of ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3- might also give a hint at how Prp43 switches into the closed conformation since in the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structure one inter-domain contact is present between the RecA2 (Asp 486) and the ratchet-like domain (Lys 605).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The open conformation in crystallo is highly unlikely to be a crystallization artefact because Prp43•ADP•BeF3- crystallized in different space groups and in divergent crystallization conditions.
source: Owing to the fact that Prp43•ADP•BeF3- crystallized in different space groups and in divergent crystallization conditions, the open conformation in crystallo is highly unlikely to be a crystallization artefact.
evidence: This is inferred from the crystallographic data showing consistent conformations across different crystal forms.

claim: The low number of crystal contacts for ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) (355.3 Å² of buried surface/1.1% of the total surface) and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(LR) (1524.3 Å²/4.7%) supports that the open conformation reflects the solution state.
source: This assumption is additionally supported by the low number of crystal contacts for the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) (355.3 Å² of buried surface/1.1% of the total surface) and the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(LR) (1524.3 Å²/4.7%) complex structure.
evidence: This is calculated from the crystal structures and used to infer that crystal packing does not significantly influence the observed conformation.

claim: The number of cysteines in ctPrp43 was determined to be 8.5 ± 0.1 and in ctPrp43-IDSB to be 9.3 ± 0.1 by Ellman reaction.
source: Via Ellman reaction, the number of cysteines was determined to be 8.5 ± 0.1 (ctPrp43) and 9.3 ± 0.1 (ctPrp43-IDSB), respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data from Ellman's reagent assay.

claim: The majority of ctPrp43-IDSB exhibits the internal disulfide bridge because oxidized cysteines cannot be detected by Ellman reaction and only the nine cysteines present in the wild-type protein were determined.
source: This allows us to conclude that the majority of ctPrp43-IDSB exhibits the internal disulfide bridge because oxidized cysteines cannot be detected by this method and only the nine cysteines, which are also present in the wild-type protein, were determined.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ellman reaction data and knowledge of the method's specificity.

claim: ctPrp43-IDSB exhibits a strongly reduced unwinding velocity (0.46 nM/min) compared to wild-type ctPrp43 (60.03 nM/min).
source: Figure 4a shows the maximal unwinding velocity for ctPrp43 (60.03 nM/min) and ctPrp43-IDSB (0.46 nM/min)
evidence: This is experimental data from the fluorescence-based helicase assay shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The intrinsic ATPase activity of ctPrp43-IDSB (5.04 min−1) is similar to wild-type ctPrp43 (1.81 min−1).
source: The intrinsic ATPase activity of ctPrp43-IDSB (5.04 min−1) is similar to the one determined for wild-type ctPrp43.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: The difference in the helicase and the ILS disassembly assay between ctPrp43 and ctPrp43-IDSB is solely caused by the impairment of the unwinding capabilities.
source: These findings confirm that the difference in the helicase and the ILS disassembly assay between ctPrp43 and ctPrp43-IDSB is solely caused by the impairment of the unwinding capabilities.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing ATPase activity (which is similar) with helicase activity (which is impaired) between wild-type and IDSB mutant.

claim: The basal ATPase activity of ctPrp43 (1.81 min−1) is very similar to its ortholog from S. cerevisiae (2.43 min−1).
source: The basal ATPase activity of ctPrp43 (1.81 min−1) is very similar to its ortholog from S. cerevisiae (2.43 min−1)
evidence: This compares experimental data from this study with cited data from Christian et al., 2014.

claim: ctPrp43 is stimulated by both ctNtr1-GP and ctPfa1-GP, but the effect by the latter is more pronounced.
source: ctPrp43 is stimulated by both, the ctNtr1-GP and the ctPfa1-GP, but the effect by the latter is more pronounced.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: ctPrp43 does not exhibit RNA-stimulated ATPase activity in the absence of a GP, which is a clear difference from S. cerevisiae Prp43.
source: A clear difference between C. thermophilum and S. cerevisiae Prp43 is that ctPrp43 does not exhibit RNA-stimulated ATPase activity in the absence of a GP.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: The ctPrp43 ATPase activity can only be induced by RNA if an additional G-patch protein is present.
source: The ctPrp43 ATPase activity can only be induced by RNA if an additional G-patch protein is present.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: The individual RecA-like domains of ctPrp43ΔN•ADP and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) superpose very well with r.m.s.d. values of 0.51 Å (RecA1) and 0.48 Å (RecA2).
source: The individual RecA-like domains of ctPrp43ΔN•ADP and ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) superpose very well with r.m.s.d. values of 0.51 Å (RecA1) and 0.48 Å (RecA2)
evidence: This is calculated from structural superposition of the crystal structures.

claim: The relative orientation of the two RecA-like domains differs by 6.5° between the ADP- and ADP•BeF3--bound states.
source: However, the relative orientation of the two RecA-like domains differs by 6.5°
evidence: This is calculated from structural superposition of the crystal structures.

claim: In the course of NTP hydrolysis, the loop harboring the conserved motif III, which is known to couple ATPase and unwinding activity, is shifted towards the RNA.
source: In the course of NTP hydrolysis, the loop harbouring the conserved motif III, which is known to couple ATPase and unwinding activity... is shifted towards the RNA.
evidence: This is observed by comparing the ADP and ADP•BeF3- structures, as shown in Figure 6.

claim: The ctPrp43-HT (0.68 nM/min) and the ctPrp43-HT&HL (0.88 nM/min) mutants exhibit a strongly impaired RNA unwinding activity compared with wild-type ctPrp43 (60.03 nM/min).
source: As shown in Figure 4a, the ctPrp43-HT (0.68 nM/min) and the ctPrp43-HT&HL (0.88 nM/min) mutants exhibit a strongly impaired RNA unwinding activity compared with wild-type ctPrp43 (60.03 nM/min)
evidence: This is experimental data from the helicase assay shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The ctPrp43-HL (61.87 nM/min) mutant shows an activity being almost equal to the wild-type protein.
source: Intriguingly, the ctPrp43-HL (61.87 nM/min) mutant shows an activity being almost equal to the wild-type protein.
evidence: This is experimental data from the helicase assay shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The high helicase activity of the ctPrp43-HL mutant indicates a different RNA translocation mechanism between the DEAH-box and DExH-box subfamilies.
source: This high helicase activity of the ctPrp43-HL mutant is in clear contrast to the results for MLE and thus indicates a different RNA translocation mechanism between the two subfamilies of DEAH-box and DExH-box helicases.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the functional data of Prp43 mutants with the published mechanism of MLE.

claim: An interaction between the Hook-Loop and the RNA, as seen in MLE, is unlikely in Prp43 because the Hook-Loop residues point at the opposite direction and do not contact the RNA.
source: This difference in the translocation mechanism is consistent with the ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- complex structure. An interaction between the Hook-Loop and the RNA, as seen in MLE, is unlikely in Prp43 because the Hook-Loop residues point at the opposite direction and do not contact the RNA
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Arg 180 and Phe 181 of the Hook-Turn directly point at the RNA, and after ATP-hydrolysis these residues are moving towards the RNA.
source: In contrast, Arg 180 and Phe 181 of the Hook-Turn directly point at the RNA, and after ATP-hydrolysis these residues are moving towards the RNA
evidence: This is observed by comparing structures and shown in Figure 7b.

claim: The Hook-Turn exhibits some flexibility since its main chain is present in two alternative conformations in the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structure.
source: The Hook-Turn exhibits some flexibility since its main chain is present in two alternative conformations in the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) complex structure.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the ctPrp43ΔN•ADP•BeF3-(HR) structure, the Hook-Turn is present as type I β-turn (47%) and type II β-turn (53%).
source: According to this structure, this β-turn is present as type I (47%) and type II (53%)
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ctPrp43-HL mutant dissociates ILSs at the wild-type protein level (~60%).
source: The ctPrp43-HL mutant dissociates ILSs at the wild-type protein level ~60%
evidence: This is experimental data from the ILS disassembly assay shown in Figure 5c and g.

claim: The activity of both ctPrp43-HT and ctPrp43-HT&HL is abolished and is similar to the background level of scILS at ~10%.
source: while the activity of both ctPrp43-HT and ctPrp43-HT&HL is abolished and is similar to the background level of scILS at ~10%
evidence: This is experimental data from the ILS disassembly assay shown in Figure 5a, f and h.

claim: Only the Hook-Turn residues are crucial for the function of Prp43 in the spliceosome, while the Hook-Loop residues are not required.
source: These data confirmed that also in the spliceosome only the Hook-Turn residues are crucial for the function of Prp43, while the Hook-Loop residues are not required.
evidence: This is inferred from the ILS disassembly assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The ctPrp43-HT mutant binds U16-RNA with a higher affinity (KD 0.84 ± 0.05 µM) than the wild-type protein (KD 4.98 ± 0.57 µM).
source: In order to address the possibility that the reduced helicase activity of the HT mutant is caused by a reduced affinity for RNA, the RNA binding was measured by means of fluorescence anisotropy revealing that this mutant is able to bind U16-RNA even with a higher affinity than the wild-type protein (KD 0.84 ± 0.05 µM vs. 4.98 ± 0.57 µM)
evidence: This is experimental data from fluorescence anisotropy measurements shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The loss of helicase activity of the HT mutant is not caused by a loss of ATPase activity since all three mutants exhibit a level of intrinsic ATPase activity comparable to wild-type Prp43.
source: Furthermore, the loss of helicase activity of the HT mutant is not caused by a loss of ATPase activity since all three mutants (ctPrp43-HT: 13.21 min−1, ctPrp43-HL: 6.19 min−1, ctPrp43-HT&HL: 7.61 min−1) exhibit a level of intrinsic ATPase activity comparable to wild-type Prp43
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: The ctPrp43-HT and ctPrp43-HT&HL mutants are not additionally stimulated by U16-RNA in contrast to the ctPrp43-HL mutant.
source: Furthermore, all of the three Hook-Turn or Hook-Loop mutants are stimulated by G-patch proteins, but it is remarkable that the ctPrp43-HT and ctPrp43-HT&HL mutants are not additionally stimulated by U16-RNA in contrast to the ctPrp43-HL mutant.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Table 3.

claim: The lack of RNA-induced stimulation for ctPrp43-HT and ctPrp43-HT&HL might hint at the fact that the ATPase activity stimulation of Prp43 by RNA occurs at the interior tunnel via the interaction with the Hook-Turn.
source: The lack of RNA-induced stimulation for these two constructs might hint at the fact that the ATPase activity stimulation of Prp43 by RNA occurs at the interior tunnel via the interaction with the Hook-Turn.
evidence: This is speculated based on the ATPase activity data and structural observations.

claim: Prp43 binds RNA in a sequence-independent manner, which is explained by the almost entire absence of interactions between the bases of the RNA and Prp43.
source: Prp43 was known to bind RNA in a sequence-independent manner which is explained by the ctPrp43ΔN•U7•ADP•BeF3- complex structure revealing the almost entire absence of interactions between the bases of the RNA and Prp43.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing lack of base-specific interactions.

claim: The observed KD value in the μM range suggests that the RNA binding of Prp43 is transient.
source: The observed KD value in the μM range suggests that the RNA binding of Prp43 is transient, which is in line with the low number of hydrogen bonds primarily formed by four out of the seven nucleotides, and the high B-factors for U1-U3 and their alternative conformations.
evidence: This is inferred from the KD measurements and structural observations.

claim: This unselective and transient binding mode of RNA by Prp43 is perfectly in line with its molecular function.
source: However, this unselective and transient binding mode of RNA by Prp43 is perfectly in line with its molecular function.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and knowledge of Prp43's diverse cellular roles.

claim: Target sites in rRNA maturation and pre-mRNA splicing are very different and thus selective RNA binding would not be compatible with Prp43's mode of function.
source: Target sites in rRNA maturation and pre-mRNA splicing are very different and thus selective RNA binding would not be compatible with Prp43's mode of function.
evidence: This is inferred from knowledge of Prp43's diverse cellular roles and the structural data.

claim: MLE binds poly-uridine RNA in a sequence-dependent manner, in contrast to Prp43.
source: Despite the fact that the architecture of the conserved domains is almost identical and the relative position of the bound RNA in the helicase is similar, MLE binds poly-uridine RNA in a sequence-dependent manner.
evidence: This is cited from Prabu et al., 2015 and compared with the Prp43 structure.

claim: Four main-chain amide interactions between residues of the RecA1 or RecA2 domains and the RNA are present in Prp43, one with each of the tightly bound nucleotides (U4-U7).
source: In Prp43, four main-chain amide interaction interactions between residues of the RecA1 or RecA2 domains and the RNA are present, one with each of the tightly bound nucleotides (U4-U7). Glu 316 interacts with U4, Gly 349 with U5, Arg 153 with U6 and Arg 180 with U7
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1e.

claim: These main-chain amide interactions are completely conserved in MLE.
source: Interestingly, these main-chain amide interactions are completely conserved in MLE. Despite the fact that the residues themselves are not conserved in MLE, the position at which the interaction takes place is virtually identical
evidence: This is determined by comparing the Prp43 structure with the MLE structure from Prabu et al., 2015, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The interactions with the conserved threonine residues (Thr 195 from motif Ib and Thr 381 from motif V) are also present in MLE.
source: Furthermore, the interactions with the conserved threonine residues are also present in MLE (Thr 486-U9 and Thr 717-U7).
evidence: This is determined by comparing the Prp43 structure with the MLE structure from Prabu et al., 2015.

claim: Three additional side chain interactions are conserved between Prp43 and MLE: Arg 201 with the ribose of U7, Asn 382 with the ribose of U4, and Lys 403 with the phosphate moiety of U4.
source: Moreover, there are three additional side chain interactions which are conserved between Prp43 and MLE. The interaction of Arg 201 (motif Ib) with the ribose of the U7, the hydrogen bonding of Asn 382 with the ribose of U4 and the interaction of Lys 403 with the phosphate moiety of U4 in Prp43 have identical counterparts in MLE.
